versions.marketingVersion: Sonic (2006) — U8 mod archive compatibility, build 1.0.8
versions.localizedDescription:
General U8 archive compatibility update for the iOS mod loader, following the “Invalid Sonic '06 U8 root (16-byte entries required)” report. This changes the shared reader for all enabled mods; there are no title- or author-specific exceptions.

- Accept validated ordinary 12-byte raw U8 nodes as well as extended 16-byte Sonic '06 nodes. Convert input into the extended game layout.
- Accept root labels and unused root/directory metadata instead of requiring every such field to be zero. Continue validating table bounds, member names, hierarchy, duplicates and payload bounds.
- Write the extended U8 compatibility marker expected by archive tools. A new cache revision regenerates archives from earlier builds.
- Identify whether an archive read error originated from the installed original, a complete replacement, or a mod archive. Keep the manager open for retries.

**Validation:** ASan/UBSan mod/archive regression suite passed, including flat/nested ordinary U8 conversion, named roots, nonzero metadata, mixed input layouts, priority, compressed payload preservation and malformed data. The public Werehog package (https://gamebanana.com/mods/330727) matching the screenshot's title/author passed import, selection and archive merging against synthetic originals; an independent decoder compared every mod member and verified preservation of an original-only member. A supplied real `shader.arc` round trip passed. Full Release arm64 iPhoneOS build and IPA integrity checks passed.

The public Werehog archive itself already passed the previous parser. The tester's installed original archive was unavailable, so the exact screenshot failure and in-game behavior remain unverified. This release addresses shared format assumptions rather than claiming every mod has been gameplay-tested. Native plugins, executable patches and custom HMM code still require ports.

**Build 1.0.8:** original `com.devz.sonic2006`, **Sonic (2006)** name and original icon PNGs verified. Keep this bundle ID when signing. The IPA is unsigned; no downloaded mod or original game archive is bundled.

Commit: `2b09bed` on `ios-mods-performance-20261015`.
SHA-256 (`Sonic06-iOS.ipa`): `1ebf3ee96b5347d15fde19afdbb5ca021a9c073c4fd369220973718f48c2f9e3`

Superseded by build 1.0.8 with the shared U8 reader compatibility update (https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/MarathonRecompilediOS/releases/tag/ios-mods-2026-10-15-u8-compat).

Replaces the blanket “Archive merging needs a Sonic ’06 port” rejection with real Sonic ’06 U8 archive merging. This is a general asset-mod implementation, not a special case for Super Sonic.

- Merge partial packed `.arc` files, extracted `.arc` directories, and extensionless extracted folders when the matching original archive exists.
- Match loose replacements against archive member paths, including members introduced by other enabled archive patches.
- Preserve untouched members and original compression; the top enabled mod wins each member conflict. Respect complete replacements and UMM `Read-only` archive paths.
- Prepare archives in the background with a “Preparing mods…” title. Errors keep the manager open so the selection can be changed and retried.
- Cache verified merged archives without modifying installed game files or imported mod assets. Preparation uses bounded payload buffers.

**App identity:** original `com.devz.sonic2006`, display name/icon **Sonic (2006)**, build **1.0.7**. Keep this bundle ID when signing to update the existing app. The IPA is unsigned and needs your sideloading signature. Game data is not included.

**Validation:** ASan/UBSan mod/archive tests passed, including independent U8/zlib decoding and a round trip of a supplied real `shader.arc`; existing port regressions passed; UIKit SDK compile and full Release arm64 iPhoneOS build passed. Packaged IPA integrity, original icon PNGs, bundle identity and required scene/Bluetooth metadata verified.

**Scope:** Sonic ’06 asset mods using the supported layouts. DLL plugins, custom HMM code, executable patches and Unleashed archive formats still require source ports. The tester’s specific Super Sonic package and gameplay with real mods have not been tested on a device. Older generated selections remain in `mod-cache`; it may be removed while the game is closed to reclaim storage.

Source commit: `49bce32` on `ios-mods-performance-20261015`.

SHA-256 (`Sonic06-iOS.ipa`): `be5965716fa3a5cd1819774d75957cccfeaae6cdc6decc5741c138eeab8fa205`

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned PAL build for iPhone and iPad. Sign the IPA with your preferred sideloading tool before installing. Supply your own matching European PAL Xbox disc; game files and music are not included. Other executable regions/revisions require matching translations.

Bundle ID: `com.devz.nfsu2` · Version: **0.3**, build **2**.

### Mobile experience

- Fullscreen landscape play with optional aspect-fit presentation.
- Uncapped presentation by default; optional FPS ceiling through `NFSU2_FPS_LIMIT`.
- 4× internal width and height by default on iOS; adjustable render scale.
- Racing-style touch controls and a separate simple menu layout. Both layouts support independent positioning, size, opacity, visibility and button mappings, with Save, Cancel and Reset.
- Automatic PAL Menu/Drive switching, including pause/options/frontend detection. A manual toggle remains available.
- Physical controllers take over from the touch pad; disconnecting restores neutral touch input.
- MP3 import from Files, persistent playlist, playback switch, volume and Next Track. Lower the original soundtrack's Music volume in-game to hear only your playlist with game effects.
- Background suspension for the game, GPU work and audio.

### Import and distribution

- Streaming Xbox ISO extraction with path/bounds checks, executable preflight, staged replacement and save preservation.
- PAL Europe and NTSC-U executable profiles. Each build contains one matching executable translation; region-neutral ISO extraction does not provide universal regional playback.
- Active extracted directory and compiled profile shown under **Edit → Game files**. Default directory: **Files → On My iPhone/iPad → NFSU2 → game**.
- New game-cover icon, display name **NFSU2**, bundle ID **com.devz.nfsu2**, version **0.3**, build **2**.
- Public unsigned PAL IPA and SHA-256 checksum in `dist/`; sign for your own device before installation.
- Public source cleaned of local developer notes and compiled test binaries. Game files, generated game code, music and signing material remain excluded from source.

### Performance

- Cache Metal uniform, constant-buffer, texture and sampler bindings within their valid encoder lifetime.
- Reuse unchanged transform-constant uploads within a command buffer; keep fresh allocations for changed constants and instanced draws.
- Combine matching feedback-stage snapshots into one copy per draw.
- Use render-pass clears for complete surface clears while preserving partial and active-pass behavior.
- Native PAL CRT/video conversion fast paths and Apple generated-code optimization.
- Add asynchronous GPU timing diagnostics without waiting for GPU completion.

### Validation and limitations

- Seven input/pacing tests passed, alongside UIKit layout/customization/lifecycle/import tests, MP3 playback tests, XISO checks and Metal GPU regression checks at native and 4× scale.
- Installed and launched on an iPhone 16 Pro Max. All 191 transferred disc files matched source sizes and SHA-1 checksums on-device.
- Synthetic constant-upload benchmarks reduced CPU submission time by about 7–9% for that workload; this is not a measured gameplay FPS gain.
- Real race/pause automatic transitions and sustained gameplay performance still need device validation. Arbitrary regions and executable revisions require their own verified translation.

apps.name: Super Smash Flash 2
apps.subtitle: Unofficial Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port with offline Ruffle runtime, customizable touch controls and gamepad
apps.localizedDescription:
Unofficial Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port with offline Ruffle runtime, customizable touch controls and gamepad support.

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/SSF2-iOS

versions.marketingVersion: SSF2 iOS 1.1.9 — Full key bindings and C-stick controls
versions.localizedDescription:
Adds the missing game-input bindings and dedicated C-stick controls.

- **KEYS** and controller action menus now include **C-Up, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, Jump 2, Shield 2 and Dash**. Key bindings may also be left unassigned.
- The right stick defaults to the four C actions, using **T / F / G / H** for up / left / down / right. A diagonal tilt selects one C direction. Old unassigned right-stick defaults migrate once; existing custom action and key mappings remain.
- Adds an adjustable stick dead zone with threshold hysteresis and optional left-stick-strength walk/dash control. Light tilt sends movement; above 75% horizontal tilt adds Dash. This provides two speed levels rather than continuous analog movement.
- Keeps the memory and audio improvements from 1.1.8. The remaining crash after several matches is unresolved; this release does not claim another memory-crash fix.

### Set up C-stick attacks

In the game's **Options → Controls → P1**, bind **C-Up = T, C-Left = F, C-Down = G, C-Right = H**. These slots initially show n/a and must be assigned in the game too. Select each slot and tilt the corresponding right-stick direction to assign it. If your port controller settings previously used **Attack** on the right stick, change those mappings to the corresponding **C** actions in **CONTROLS → CONTROLLER**.

For optional walk/dash, bind the game's **Dash** to **Shift**, disable **Auto-Dash** and **D-Tap Dash**, then enable **Left-stick strength controls walk / dash** in the port. To assign an n/a slot on iPhone, map a controller button to that action, select the slot in the game, and press that button.

The portable Flash movie disables its desktop controller initialization. The iOS port still uses a GameController-to-keyboard bridge, so the in-game device list remains **Keyboard**. Native XInput and continuous analog movement are not enabled by this update.

Validation: Controller checks passed for native and browser paths, all C directions, independent movement, diagonal direction choice, custom/disabled keys, additional jump/shield/dash actions, migration, dead-zone hysteresis and disconnect releases. A macOS WebKit integration check assigned all four C slots to T/F/G/H using injected native-controller updates. Audio, rendering, cache, recovery and loader-patch regressions passed. The unsigned Release IPA passed its audit, and every bundled web/game/runtime file was compared with verified source. Physical controller/iPhone validation is still needed.

Download **SuperSmashFlash2-1.1.9-unsigned.ipa**, sign it and install it. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier (`com.devz.supersmashflash2`) to retain your data.

versions.marketingVersion: SSF2 iOS 1.1.8 — Sequential loading and binary sprite cache
versions.localizedDescription:
Addresses startup memory pressure, loading stalls and audio interruptions following version 1.1.7.

- Sprite storage now uses binary requests over the existing offline URL scheme. It no longer uses JavaScript prompts, which interrupted Web Audio during loading, or makes base64/JSON copies of every sprite.
- Enables SSF2's existing sequential resource loader to reduce overlapping asset decoding. The checksum-verified original stays intact; a derived iOS movie changes exactly one boolean instruction. Both Xcode and packaged builds load the derived movie.
- Native cache failures show recovery instead of silently building a large RAM cache.
- Preserves the repeated-Resume fix and existing touch layouts, saves and controls.

Validation: Two successful macOS WebKit startup traces completed at approximately 624 MB of WebAssembly allocation, compared with approximately 784 MB in the old-build trace. This measures WebAssembly allocation, not total process memory. The title/menu responded, a Ness/Mario battle loaded, and an output-graph probe detected a nonzero audio signal. A UIKit Mac Catalyst test passed 1,000 byte-exact binary cache round trips, 500 transient lifecycle/audio notifications, background suspension and one-tap resume. JavaScript, native cache and deterministic one-instruction loader-patch checks passed, as did the unsigned Release IPA audit. Every bundled web/game/runtime file was compared with the verified source.

Physical iPhone startup reliability, headphone output and longer-session stability still need verification. This release does not establish that all underlying memory-related crashes are eliminated. Match memory remains substantial. Restart after WebKit termination still returns to the title and cannot restore a lost match.

Download **SuperSmashFlash2-1.1.8-unsigned.ipa**, sign it and install it with your sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier (`com.devz.supersmashflash2`) to preserve existing data.

versions.marketingVersion: SSF2 iOS 1.1.7 — Resume loop fix and lower startup memory
versions.localizedDescription:
Fixes the repeated **Game suspended / RESUME** interruptions reported after the audio update, and reduces startup memory pressure.

- Only app backgrounding shows the native port's Resume card. Audio interruptions, headphone route notifications and transient inactivity no longer suspend the game.
- Removes the audio activation feedback path. Playback policy is configured before audio starts; taps and key presses continue to unlock Web Audio.
- Background suspension is idempotent and still offers Resume when Ruffle has already paused itself. Backgrounding before the first start preserves LET'S PLAY.
- New installations use lower-memory rendering by default. The low-memory GPU sprite cache now targets 64 MB instead of 96 MB.
- Packaging clones Web resources directly into the IPA on APFS, avoiding another full asset copy in DerivedData.

Validation: JavaScript control, audio, rendering, texture-cache and recovery checks passed, including native visibility regression and a 64 MB disk-backed cache. A UIKit Mac Catalyst check of the shipped native controller passed 1,000 trusted cache prompts and 500 transient lifecycle/audio notifications without pausing, then background pause and one-tap resume. Native texture-storage checks and the unsigned Release IPA audit passed. All bundled web/game/runtime files were compared with the verified source.

**Device validation:** The repeated suspension paths have been removed and regression-tested. The reported startup WebKit termination and physical iPhone/headphone behavior still need checking on affected devices; this release does not establish that every memory-related crash is eliminated.

Download **SuperSmashFlash2-1.1.7-unsigned.ipa**, sign it with your sideloading tool and install it. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier (`com.devz.supersmashflash2`) to preserve existing data. Restart after a terminated WebKit process returns to the title; it cannot recover the lost match.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.6 (build 9) fixes missing audio unlock and an unreliable restart control.

- User taps and key presses explicitly resume the Web Audio contexts used by Ruffle. The custom Play button unlocks audio before starting the game loop.
- Ruffle's unmute overlay is visible as a fallback.
- The native playback audio session is activated and reactivated when appropriate. Headphone disconnection pauses the game; connection, app activation and interruptions are handled.
- The native Restart game button has an explicit layout width and remains enabled while a replacement page loads. Brief duplicate taps are debounced without disabling the control.

A restart creates a new Flash runtime and returns to the title screen. It cannot restore a match from a terminated process. Completed save data and control settings remain in the persistent store. This release does not establish that the earlier memory-related crashes have been eliminated.

Validation: audio unlock, interruption and gesture-retry tests; touch, renderer and cache checks; source/IPA audits; unsigned iOS Release build. The shipped recovery-view component accepted two successive taps in a UIKit Mac Catalyst test app. A native WebKit probe reached a running audio context, but non-silent headphone output still needs verification on affected iPhones.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign it with your sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.5 (build 8) adds native recovery from a failed game page.

- A native Restart game screen handles WebKit process termination, WebGL context loss and sprite-cache read failures. It remains available even when the web controls have disappeared or a failure occurs in the background.
- Restart replaces the WebView, stops the old controller bridge and clears temporary sprite storage. The persistent save-data store remains in use.
- Committed navigation failures are handled as well as provisional failures. Slow restarts allow another attempt after 30 seconds; this does not limit gameplay time.
- Failed sessions require a deliberate restart rather than silently reloading into another failure.

There is no play-time limit. Free storage does not prevent RAM or graphics-memory pressure. This release improves recovery; it does not establish or eliminate every underlying crash. An interrupted match cannot be recovered.

Validation: graphics-loss and cache-read failure notification tests; texture-cache, pixel round-trip, touch and rendering checks; source and IPA audits; unsigned iOS Release build. Native recovery still needs verification on the affected iPhone.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign it with your sideloading tool. Use the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.4 (build 7) reduces memory pressure during startup and character/stage changes.

- Compressed sprites move to temporary native disk storage instead of staying in the JavaScript heap. The WebKit integration test paged approximately 326 MB of compressed sprites to disk.
- Inactive static sprite textures leave a bounded GPU working set and restore through stable logical handles. The target is 128 MB normally, 96 MB on low-memory startup and 64 MB after a memory warning; active draw inputs and modified render targets are preserved.
- Sampler settings, texture-unit bindings and pixel-store state survive restoration.
- Local asset responses use no-store to avoid retaining response bodies in the browser cache.
- The native cache is session-only, reuses freed storage and disappears on app exit.

Keep at least 1 GB of device storage free for normal play; long sessions can require more. If temporary storage cannot be used, compressed sprites fall back to RAM.

Validation: 48-sprite cache stress tests with both RAM and native paging, exact pixel restoration, multiple WebGL contexts, native storage tests, touch/rendering checks, source and IPA audits, and an unsigned iOS Release build. A native macOS WebKit test started a Ness battle, switched to Link and another stage, and reached the next battle without a process termination or sprite-cache read error.

This addresses identified memory pressure, but all crashes on affected iPhones have not yet been verified as resolved. Ruffle can still retain other movie resources.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign it with your sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS 1.1.3 (build 6) fixes touch layout editing and reduces memory pressure.

- Pause and Start / OK use Space; old Enter pause bindings migrate automatically.
- MENU replaces the Escape-based Back button and opens the app control panel.
- D-pad dragging supports upward movement, pointer capture, resizing and reset.
- Fullscreen landscape play is enabled by default, with overlay controls.
- Deferred textures release their original pixel buffers; upload buffers are reused and rendering resolution is capped.
- Memory warnings or WebKit process termination enable persistent lower-memory rendering, with a controlled retry after repeated failure.

The IPA is unsigned. Sign and install it with your preferred sideloading tool. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier to preserve existing app data.

Validation: JavaScript control, memory-retention and rendering tests; source and IPA privacy audits; unsigned iOS Release build. Simultaneous-KO crashes still need testing on physical iPhones; the memory fixes cannot guarantee every device avoids iOS memory limits.

First public release of the Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port.

- Offline Super Smash Flash 2 v1.3.1.2 Portable, with bundled Ruffle 0.6.0.
- Matching multitouch control deck, adjustable size and opacity, and separate customizable portrait/landscape layouts.
- Native gamepad support and remappable touch, keyboard, and controller actions.
- Deferred compressed texture uploads to reduce GPU memory use.
- Clean public source with checksum-pinned asset downloads and reproducible unsigned IPA packaging.
- Release builds exclude the device test command channel, diagnostic files, source maps, signing files, and embedded local build paths.

**Installation:** Requires iOS/iPadOS 16 or later. Download the unsigned IPA, sign it with your preferred sideloading tool, and install. Preserve the bundle identifier and signing identity when updating to keep app data.

The game runs offline; online multiplayer is unsupported. Performance and Flash compatibility depend on the device and Ruffle.

**Validation:** Xcode Release build, touch/controller/layout tests, texture memory tests, source privacy audit, and final IPA integrity/privacy audit passed. The SHA-256 checksum is attached.

See the README for controls, installation, building, credits, and licenses.

versions.marketingVersion: NativePorts 0.2.2 — SSF2T and Slam n Jam fixes
versions.localizedDescription:
SSF2T and Slam n Jam 0.2.2

iOS and Windows builds passed. iOS IPAs are unsigned; sign/install with ESign, keeping the existing bundle identifiers.

Slam n Jam: startup asks for keyboard 1 or controller Start, with no coin prompt. Restart reads RESTART GAME. PS1 Select is available as Select (keyboard Tab, controller View); old settings migrate. Native gameplay canvas expands from 320 to 426 columns instead of stretching. Original-size sprites, text and HUD remain centered; textures live in original VRAM and expanded framebuffers use separate banks. CRT behavior is unchanged.

SSF2T: reflected edge artwork removed. The visible gameplay window narrows symmetrically as the camera approaches finite stage boundaries, returning to the original 384 columns at either limit. It expands away from those limits. Menus keep their original proportions centered in a 512-column frame with colored sides.

Validation: iOS and Windows builds, controller suite, canvas isolation and stage-boundary tests passed. Real Slam gameplay toggled 320 -> 426 -> 320 columns; all 81,920 pixels of the central original view matched the same saved frame exactly. Real SSF2T gameplay captures returned to 384 columns at both edges, and menu captures were 512 columns with colored margins. Device-specific iPhone and Windows gameplay still needs retesting.

No game files or game screenshots are included. SSF2T and Slam n Jam are version 0.2.2. The unchanged THPS2 and UMK3 version 0.2.1 builds are also included here. Download NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip for all four current Windows builds; the smaller SSF2T-SlamJam96 ZIP contains only those two games. BUILD-VERSIONS.txt inside the complete ZIP identifies every game version.

- Four unsigned iOS IPAs: sign and install using ESign.
- Windows x64 ZIP: contains all four games and required SDL libraries.
- SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the downloadable builds.

Existing bundle identifiers are preserved. Game files are not included. NBA Showtime remains unfinished and is not included.

### Validation and remaining checks

All four iOS and Windows builds passed. Controller, VRAM, GTE projection and stage-edge regression checks passed; 92 Dreamcast shader variants compiled and linked. A local Slam ’n Jam gameplay capture showed complete crowd rendering in one tested camera.

THPS2 iPhone frame-rate improvement and HUD placement still need device confirmation. Slam ’n Jam shot-clock readability and other cameras, plus affected SSF2T and UMK3 stages, still need gameplay retesting. Native PS1 resolution is unchanged. SSF2T edge scenery uses reflected existing artwork.

- Uses the supplied game artwork for each iOS app and Windows executable/window icon. Keeps unique bundle IDs unchanged to preserve installed game data.
- Adds game-specific widescreen patches for SSF2T, UMK3 and Slam ’n Jam ’96, alongside the existing Flycast widescreen patch for THPS2. Widescreen can be toggled in display settings.
- Updates aspect-ratio handling and NewPixie CRT rendering to preserve picture edges. CRT filtering remains enabled by default and can be disabled.
- Refreshes cached core sources before builds so source changes rebuild the embedded engine.
- Includes touch controls and remappable multiplayer controller support on both platforms.

Download one unsigned IPA per game and sign it with your sideloading tool. For Windows, extract NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip and keep each EXE beside its SDL2.dll. Use your own game files; ROMs, disc images and signing credentials are not included.

Known limitations: THPS2 on iOS uses an interpreter and may run below full speed. Slam ’n Jam ’96 can leave dark corners in some widescreen camera angles. NBA Showtime remains frontend-only and is not included.

Validation: all four iOS build logs report success; Windows binaries were packaged from the latest local builds. Virtual controller tests passed for all five frontends, along with ROM-import checks, basketball action tests and both THPS2 texture-cache configurations. These checks do not establish full-speed performance or physical multiplayer operation on every device. SHA256SUMS.txt contains asset checksums.

Super Street Fighter II Turbo 0.1.1, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 0.1.1, Slam 'n Jam '96 0.1.1 and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 0.1.9 for iOS and Windows. Unsigned IPAs for sideloading (ESign, AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly) and a Windows x64 package. No game files are included; see the README for what you need.

# Sonic Unleashed for iOS v1.1.0 — Native Mod Manager

## Changelog

- Added a native startup mod manager with folder import through Files.
- Enable or disable mods, reorder priority, and preserve selections across launches.
- Check dependency IDs and minimum numeric versions before starting.
- Toggle the built-in game codes from the manager.
- Connect selections to the existing asset replacements, append archives, loose files, UMM merges, and mod save redirection.
- Display unsupported DLL and custom HMM script requirements.
- Confine mod include/save paths and reject symbolic links.
- Compile the game Metal shader cache for iOS 15 with the iPhone SDK.
- Target iOS 15 for bundled dependencies and use numeric bundle versions.
- Add an IPA packaging helper for builds made with the Ninja preset.

## Install and use

Download `SonicUnleashed_iOS_v1.1.0.ipa` and re-sign it with your sideloading tool before installation. This IPA has an ad-hoc signature and no Apple provisioning profile. Supply your own runtime game assets through Files.

Extract an Unleashed Recompiled mod, launch the app, tap **Import folder**, and select the folder containing `mod.ini`. Enable it, set its priority, and tap **Play**. New imports start disabled. The first mod wins file replacement conflicts.

ARM64 iPhone/iPad build targeting iOS 15 or later. DLL plugins and arbitrary HMM scripts need individual iOS ports; this release does not promise compatibility with every mod. There is no online mod catalog or automatic downloading.

## MCX360 Edition 1.1

### New
- **On-screen touch controls**, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with `touch_controls`, `touch_controls_opacity` and `touch_haptics` in `mc360.toml`.
- **Save thumbnails**: your worlds now show a picture in the world list.
- **Exit Game** now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen.

### Performance
- Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds.
- Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (`framerate_limit`, default 60).
- The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores.
- Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame.

### Fixes
- Fixed random crashes after playing for a while.
- Fixed choppy audio.
- Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed.
- Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing.

### Known issues
- Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps.
- The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save.
- Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement.

Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.
First iOS release.
